result.note: Tests the change in silver's import policy status, its coverage, and the preceding duty hike, all of which are trade policy measures linked to forex pressure.

questions.prompt: In May 2026, India changed its import policy for silver. Consider the following statements:
items: Silver imports were moved from the "free" to the "restricted" category, so importers now need prior government approval.
The new rules cover only silver jewellery, leaving silver bars of 99.9% purity freely importable.
The move followed an increase in the duty on gold and silver from 6% to 15% announced earlier the same week.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The rules cover silver bars of 99.9% purity and all other semi-manufactured forms, which together made up more than 90% of silver imports the previous fiscal year. The measures aim to curb precious metals imports amid pressure on foreign exchange reserves from the Strait of Hormuz crisis.
questions.source: On Saturday, India reclassified silver imports from "free" to "restricted" with immediate effect, requiring importers to obtain prior government approval before bringing in shipments.
